(11 November 2014) | attendance = 1,590,292 | average attendance = 24,357{{cite news|title=ISL Gives Indian Football a Re-launch Pad|url=http://www.newindianexpress.com/sport/ISL-Gives-Indian-Football-a-Re-launch-Pad/2014/12/21/article2582237.ece|access-date=31 May 2015|work=The New Indian Express|date=21 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008032119/http://www.newindianexpress.com/sport/ISL-Gives-Indian-Football-a-Re-launch-Pad/2014/12/21/article2582237.ece|archive-date=8 October 2015|url-status=dead}} | prevseason = | nextseason = [[2015 Indian Super League|2015]] | dates = 12 October – 20 December }} The '''2014 Hero Indian Super League''' was the first season of the [[Indian Super League]], the top flight [[association football|football]] league of [[Football in India|India]]. The season featured eight teams, each playing 14 matches during the regular season. The regular season started on 12 October when [[Atlético de Kolkata]] defeated [[Mumbai City FC|Mumbai City]] 3–0 at the [[Salt Lake Stadium]] in [[Kolkata]].{{cite news|last1=Dutta|first1=Subhasish|title=ISL 2014: Slick Atletico de Kolkata thump Mumbai City FC 3-0 in opener|url=http://www.ibnlive.com/footballnext/news/isl-2014-slick-atletico-de-kolkata-thump-mumbai-city-fc-30-in-opener-505703-5-21.html|access-date=31 May 2015|work=IBN Live|date=14 October 2014|archive-date=30 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330150924/https://www.news18.com/|url-status=live}} The season ended on 20 December when Atlético de Kolkata defeated the [[Kerala Blasters FC|Kerala Blasters]] in the [[2014 Indian Super League final|final]] 1–0 in front of 36,484 spectators.{{cite news|title=ISL: Atletico de Kolkata beat Kerala Blasters 1-0 to win title|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-Atletico-de-Kolkata-beat-Kerala-Blasters-1-0-to-win-title/articleshow/45588313.cms|access-date=31 May 2015|work=The Times of India|date=20 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190811014545/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-Atletico-de-Kolkata-beat-Kerala-Blasters-1-0-to-win-title/articleshow/45588313.cms|archive-date=11 August 2019|url-status=live}} [[Mohammed Rafique (footballer)|Mohammed Rafique]] was the lone goalscorer as the Kolkata club became the inaugural champions. ==Teams== {{location map+ |India |float=right |width=350 |alt=Locations of the ISL Teams |caption=Locations of the ISL Teams |places= {{location map~ |India |lat=22.56972 |long=88.36972 |label=

The first draft would be to sign the initial 14 Indian players and then the second one would be to sign seven foreign players.{{cite news|title=Indian Super League football: Major signings on day 1 of players draft|url=http://www.oneindia.com/sports/indian-super-league-major-signings-on-day-1-players-draft-1487553.html|access-date=2 June 2015|work=One India|date=22 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208092154/http://www.oneindia.com/sports/indian-super-league-major-signings-on-day-1-players-draft-1487553.html|archive-date=8 December 2015|url-status=live}} ====Domestic players draft==== {{More information|2014 ISL Inaugural Domestic Draft}} The domestic players draft took place within two days on 22 July and 23 July 2014 in [[Mumbai]].{{cite news|last1=Mergulhao|first1=Marcus|title=ISL domestic draft to include 40 national players|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-domestic-draft-to-include-40-national-players/articleshow/38661087.cms|access-date=2 June 2015|work=The Times of India|date=19 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708092736/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-domestic-draft-to-include-40-national-players/articleshow/38661087.cms|archive-date=8 July 2015|url-status=live}} There were 84 players up for grabs during the draft that could be selected between six of the eight Indian Super League teams ([[FC Goa|Goa]] and [[NorthEast United FC|NorthEast United]] selected from their respective [[I-League]] teams). Close to 50% of the 84 players had played for [[India national football team|India]] internationally. The opening pick in the draft was [[Lenny Rodrigues]] by [[FC Pune City]]. [[Subrata Pal]], [[Syed Nabi]], and [[Gouramangi Singh]] were the most expensive picks during the draft. ====International draft==== {{More information|2014 ISL Inaugural International Draft}} After the completion of the domestic draft, the international draft took place on 21 August 2014, also in [[Mumbai]].{{cite news|last1=Mergulhao|first1=Marcus|title=ISL: Draft for overseas players on August 21|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-Draft-for-overseas-players-on-August-21/articleshow/40244205.cms|access-date=2 June 2015|work=The Times of India|date=14 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141021105648/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/ISL-Draft-for-overseas-players-on-August-21/articleshow/40244205.cms|archive-date=21 October 2014|url-status=live}} There were 49 players available for selection during the draft.
